## TL;DR

- Started with a [Commodore 64][1] and an [Amiga][2], built my own PCs and broke a few Linux installs.
- Studied Economics, Business Administration and Computer Science in the Netherlands ([Maastricht][9]) and Sweden ([Jönköping][10]). Learned [Python][11] along the way.
- Worked on [BI][13] and [MLOps][15] at [Generali][12], including a stint in Milan, then built the MLOps team at [Covestro][18].
- After Covestro, I founded [byteCare][22] and worked as a consultant at qdive (now [Wavestone][23]) and [Comma Soft][24].
- Today I work on AI engineering and AI infrastructure at byteCare.

## The early days

My first computers were a [Commodore 64][1] and an [Amiga][2] in the 1980s. I remember swapping floppy disks, trying to get [RAM expansions][3] to work and drawing pixel art in Paintbrush on Windows 3.11.

At some point using computers wasn't enough. I wanted to know how they worked, so I built my own PCs and fought with Windows ME and 2000. I saved up for a [3DFX Voodoo][4] graphics card, so games finally looked good.

My first *programming* happened in config files. I tweaked `autoexec.cfg` and `config.cfg` to get a few more frames per second out of [Counter-Strike][5]. That got me into competitive gaming in the [ESL][6]: an [Elsa 56k modem][7], heavy CRT monitors carried to LAN parties and matches organized on [IRC][8], long before Discord.

I also tried Linux early on (SuSE, later Ubuntu) and, of course, accidentally wiped my entire hard drive :shrug:.

## University

I didn't want to study computer science in isolation, so I chose a degree combining Economics, Business Administration and Computer Science. I studied in the Netherlands ([Maastricht][9]) and Sweden ([Jönköping][10]), which came with a few memorable tech moments:

- **iPhone:** My first smartphone was an iPhone 3GS. Having maps and mobile internet in my pocket was a big deal.
- **Spotify:** It launched while I was in Sweden. I wanted it so badly that I asked a fellow student I had just met to sign me up with his credit card, because I didn't own one yet.
- **Mac:** On my flight to Sweden, the airline destroyed my Windows laptop. So I bought a Mac. Haven't switched back since.

This is also when I learned [Python][11], my first real programming language. I still use and love it today.

## Career

### Generali

I started my career at [Generali][12] as a technical project manager in [Business Intelligence][13]. I soon moved closer to the infrastructure and helped introduce [Hadoop][14] as part of Generali's data architecture. BI taught me that whatever you build, a big part of the work is cleaning and shaping data.

In Milan (Italy), I led the implementation of Generali's first ML-powered business process. Besides the tech, that meant a lot of project management and getting the people involved on board. Training the model was the easy part. Running it reliably in production was hard, so I moved into [MLOps][15] and worked a lot with [Kubernetes][16] and [OpenShift][17], before MLOps was a common term.

### Covestro

At [Covestro][18], I built the MLOps team and platform from scratch, running entirely on AWS with CI/CD pipelines and infrastructure as code. Besides Python, I started using [Terraform][19], and [Go][20] or [TypeScript][21] when a project needed it.

### Consulting and byteCare

After Covestro, I founded [byteCare][22] and moved into consulting, first as Lead AI Engineer at qdive (now part of [Wavestone][23]) and then as Principal Consultant for MLOps at [Comma Soft][24], helping clients build and run their ML and AI platforms.

Today I work on byteCare full-time. My focus is AI engineering and AI infrastructure: platforms that run LLM-based applications and assistants in production. I help organizations use AI that is cost-effective, performant and privacy-preserving, without giving up control over their data or blowing their infrastructure budget.

## What drives me

I like taking things apart to see how they work, and then building something useful with them. That was true for the Amiga and it's true for AI platforms. The tools change every few years. That part hasn't.

## Get in touch

Want to chat? Reach out on [LinkedIn][25]. You'll find my code on [GitHub][26] and my talks on the [Talks](talks.qmd) page.
